summary: Tucked into a narrow canyon at the base of the western slope of Mount Tamalpais, Fairfax occupies just 2.2 square miles of densely wooded terrain where redwoods and live oaks press right up against the backyards of homes — the kind of place where deer on your driveway is a Tuesday. The town's single commercial corridor along Broadway and Bolinas Road functions as a genuine village center with independent coffee shops, a natural foods grocery, and restaurants that lean heavily toward organic and vegetarian — an identity so distinct it would be nearly impossible to confuse with any other Marin County town. With a median home price of $1,121,500 against a median household income of $131,875, the price-to-income ratio sits around 8.5×, meaning even upper-middle-income earners face serious leverage to buy. Fairfax is emphatically a bedroom community; most workers commute east toward San Rafael, San Francisco, or the broader Bay Area, since the local economy runs on small retail and services. The climate is remarkably mild — annual highs averaging 68°F with nine hours of daily sunshine — though the canyon geography means fog lingers on summer mornings longer than in neighboring ridgetop towns. Trail access is extraordinary: routes into open-space preserves and up Mount Tamalpais start essentially at the town's edge. The defining tension is a place that offers genuine small-town walkability and immediate wilderness but prices that reflect its proximity to one of the most expensive metro areas on Earth.
